rejected_release_candidates.reason: The Mac bundle omitted share/apple-identity, so Companion dependency resolution failed before iPhone signing and the UI collapsed the failure into an unactionable Apple Account message.

Owner-attended first-open acceptance found that the app entered device setup without first welcoming the person, explaining the intention-to-native-iPhone-app relationship, or giving enough plain-language purpose for each prerequisite.

Owner-attended Registry acceptance found that the Mac app rejected valid local Registry responses and exposed neither CLI activation nor the init, deploy, Companion-approval, and recipient-signing path, leaving the person unable to begin the end-to-end Ship walkthrough.

Owner-attended init acceptance found that the CLI abandoned its local adoption request after ten seconds while Xcode correctly continued the real Simulator build, falsely reporting a connection error and hiding all subsequent progress.

Owner-attended deploy acceptance found that the publication scanner treated the short byte prefix ghp_ inside compressed PNG data as a complete credential and rejected safe source before Companion approval.
RC6 predates deploy-time signed app slugs, authenticated global-alias review, the exact friend handoff page, and the private intended-phone selector required for this real Ship-to-friend mission.

The owner-attended Ship exposed two live client blockers: the Mac compared the constructor-patched Registry runtime against the template hash instead of the threshold-signed activation, and whole-response source downloads were unreliable at real app size. The live Builder-authorized Ship was reconciled after focused fixes, but RC7 is not the friend-install candidate.
RC8 predates signed public app icons and screenshots, the canonical Ship/Fork/Claim website timeline, and the exact Claim handoff implemented for the current real-user path.
